study_info.title: Virtual reality intervention in postoperative rehabilitation after total knee arthroplasty: a prospective and randomized controlled clinical trial
study_info.authors: Chi Jin, Yongjian Feng, Yongjian Ni, Zhonglin Shan
study_info.study_design: prospective and randomized controlled clinical trial; randomization method not detailed
study_info.inclusion_criteria: 1) Patients diagnosed as OA according to The Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of Osteoarthritis issued by the Chinese Rheumatology Association in 2010; 2) Patients undergoing unilateral TKA for the first time; 3) Patients were informed about the study and informed consent was obtained; 4) The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Cangzhou Central Hospital, Cangzhou, China.
study_info.exclusion_criteria: 1) Overweight (BMI ≥30 kg/m²); 2) Severe osteoporosis; 3) Ligament injury or periprosthetic fracture occurring during TKA; 4) Unstable vital signs, complications of incisio
study_info.study_setting: Central Hospital of Cangzhou City, Cangzhou, China
study_info.source_of_recruitment: OA patients undergoing unilateral TKA at Cangzhou Central Hospital from March 2015 to October 2016

minimal_units.intervention_details: VR (Mide Technology Inc., Cangzhou, China) intervention was applied in the experimental group beginning the second day after TKA. Patients were asked to row a boat using knee flexion (interaction of VR) in an immersive virtual environment for 30 minute periods, three times a day.

minimal_units.control_details: Patients in the control group were asked to flex their knees passively using their arms until pain tolerance was reached. They held that position for 20 seconds followed by relaxing for 40 seconds. Patients were required to perform three sets of 30 repetitions daily.

meta_analysis_parameters.outcome_domain: Pain intensity (Visual Analog Scale, VAS);Disease-specific functional indices (DSI; Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index [WOMAC], Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score [KOOS]);Balance ability;Postural stability parameters;Global proprioception;Knee flexion–extension range of motion (ROM);Active knee flexion angle;Five-Times Sit-to-Stand Test (5×STS) completion time;Gait-related parameters (knee extension moment, functional weight-bearing symmetry);Walking speed;Timed standing task completion time;Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS) score;Activities-specific Balance Confidence (ABC) scale score;Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) knee score;Rehabilitation program adherence;Hospital readmission rate;Patient satisfaction;Healthcare costs.
